chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who confessed against himself to a hadd punishment, but did not specify which hadd it was, he said:
“It is ordered that he be flogged until he himself is the one who stops the hadd from being carried out against himself.”

key_terms.بِحَدٍّ: to a hadd punishment, a fixed legal penalty
key_terms.عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: against his own person, meaning self-incriminating admission
key_terms.وَلَمْ يُسَمِّ: and he did not specify or name

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone confesses to a hadd offense without specifying which hadd he committed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who confesses that he is liable for a hadd punishment without clarifying which specific offense he committed. The ruling indicates that a lesser form of punishment is applied until the person himself halts the process, reflecting caution in implementing fixed penal punishments when the confession lacks specification.
